posts.author: HoloM
posts.content_md:
I have a big rainbow type multiplexhologram (similar to the holograms made by Lloyd Cross, maybe it's one from him). This hologram has an mark on the right half of the hologram. The area is about 2x7cm where the image is damaged. 

The hologram is between two thin plastic plates to get the right geometry for viewing (bent to a half circle). I assume that condense water between this plates has swollen the emulsion , i think it didn't dry equal so the image is damaged in this area. Some parts are visible equally bright to the normal picture but somewhat distorted, and you can see the contours of the water mark. Some part of the area are also a little bit milky with the image being dimmer there. 

So the question is what to do 

Do you think this mark could be repaired with rewatering and redrying? 

Or with rebleaching? Or is it better to leave it as it is? Is the risk to high to damage it even more? Any suggestions?

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: I have heard of re-bleaching to save holograms that have printout but I don't think this would be helpful. I have often soaked holograms in water and redried them. This is pretty safe. If you can get the film separate from the plastic this would be a good choice. Make sure to post the results.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
This may not be safe though. It all depends on how the hologram was made and how it was stored...

See [http://holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=3955](http://holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=3955) for relevant info

posts.author: pearlv
posts.content_md:
Just to add my bit - I would really NOT recommend trying to re-bleach an old hologram - I saw a 30 x 40cm reflection hologram that was about 10 years old disappear that way - only because we didn't know exactly what chemistry was used to bleach the hologram in the first place. 

Unless you are quite prepared to let the hologram go I wouldn't try doing anything to it. If you do want to try recovering it I would rewash with distilled water and dry naturally.

Pearl

posts.author: HoloM
posts.content_md: So do you think also rewashing and redrying would be a risk to loose the whole hologram?

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
It can be. I've tried that with a few of my own and the emulsion has come off in the water.

Dinesh has also had that happen.

As I understand it, it all depends on how it was processed and how it was stored.

If you're set on experimenting you could try putting a drop of water somewhere outside the image and see what effect it has on the emulsion. I probably wouldn't do it if I were in your place.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Now this is purely speculative but why try to "fix" then entire hologram? If just a small part of the hologram is damaged, why not just take an eydropper or a cotton swab and just wet the damaged area and let dry? Basically, just try to fix the bad spot or at least just experiement on just a very small portion of the bad spot. But I also would be careful not to damage the hologram by simply taking it out of it's plastic plates either.

Again, I agree, personally I would never attempt to do anything to a vintage hologram, I have heard horror stories as Michael pointed out. I just thought I would share a thought if you were fixed on the idea of trying something.

If just a small part of the hologram is damaged, why not just take an eydropper or a cotton swab and just wet the damaged area and let dry? Basically, just try to fix the bad spot or at least just experiement on just a very small portion of the bad spot. But I also would be careful not to damage the hologram by simply taking it out of it's plastic plates either.Again, I agree, personally I would never attempt to do anything to a vintage hologram, I have heard horror stories as Michael pointed out. I just thought I would share a thought if you were fixed on the idea of trying something.

One reason not to try to fix one spot is that generally it won't dry back to the same thickness as the rest of the hologram. That's why wetting agents and squeegees are used as the final step. To ensure that the emulsion dries evenly.

posts.author: HoloM
posts.content_md: Just want to let you know, that I tried to rewash the "shower girl" hologram (mentioned in the holotalk) yesterday. in the first it seemed to work good. By washing, the emulsion got light milky. Then I wanted to dry it.... It would have been better if only hanged it up and let it dry in the air.... But no, i tried to dry it with a drying machine. But the emulsion was so weak that the rolls of the drying mashine scratched the emulsion and took some of the emulsion away... So I think this was my first and last attempt to rewash a nearly historic hologramm. now it's even more damaged than before. And this shurely can't be recovered. The image is visible in some places but most parts of the emulsion are damged.
